3.4.1.4-r1.burton_quote: that there were not such ordinary showers in Winter, the ripening heat in Summer, so seasonable Springs, fruitful Autumns, no marble mines in the mountains, less gold and silver than of old

3.4.1.4-r2.burton_quote: one did, that was much affected with Music, and to hear Boys sing, but very superstitious; an old Sibyl coming to his house, or an holy woman (as that place yields many), took him down for it, and told him, that in that other world he should suffer for it; thereupon he flung his rich and costly Instruments which he had bedecked with Jewels, all at once into the fire

3.4.1.4-r3.burton_quote: And for such-like toys, some so miserably afflict themselves, to despair, and death itself, rather than offend, and think themselves good Christians in it, when as indeed they are superstitious Jews

3.4.1.4-r4.burton_quote: We are tortured in Germany with these Popish edicts, our bodies so taken down, our goods so diminished, that if God had not sent Luther, a worthy man, in time to redress these mischiefs, we should have eaten hay with our horses before this
